sanskrit: tatra mallā naṭā jhallā granthikāḥ saukhaśāyikāḥ sūtamāgadhasaṃghāś cāpy astuvan vai janārdanam kuruvaṃśas tavākhyābhir āśīrbhir bharatarṣabha
english: There the wrestlers, the actors, the boxers, the reciters of legends, and those skilled in pleasant attendance, together with the throngs of bards and panegyrists, praised Janārdana, O bull of the Bharatas, blessing your house, the line of Kuru, with the recital of its glories.

sanskrit: utthāya tu yathākālam uttarā yadunandanam abhyavādayata prītā saha putreṇa bhārata tatas tasyai dadau prīto bahuratnaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: Rising at the proper hour, Uttarā, glad at heart, saluted the joy of the Yadus together with her son, O Bhārata; and well pleased, he gave to her in particular abundant jewels.

sanskrit: tathānye vṛṣṇiśārdūlā nāma cāsyākarot prabhuḥ pitus tava mahārāja satyasaṃdho janārdanaḥ
english: And so did the other tigers of the Vṛṣṇis; and the lord Janārdana, faithful to his word, conferred a name upon your father, O great king.

sanskrit: parikṣīṇe kule yasmāj jāto 'yam abhimanyujaḥ parikṣid iti nāmāsya bhavatv ity abravīt tadā
english: "Since this son of Abhimanyu has been born when the lineage had dwindled away, let his name be Parīkṣit," he said then.

sanskrit: so 'vardhata yathākālaṃ pitā tava narādhipa manaḥprahlādanaś cāsīt sarvalokasya bhārata
english: In due season your father grew, O ruler of men, and he was a delight to the hearts of all the world, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: māsajātas tu te vīra pitā bhavati bhārata athājagmuḥ subahulaṃ ratnam ādāya pāṇḍavāḥ
english: When your father was a month old, O hero, O Bhārata, the Pāṇḍavas arrived, bringing very great store of jewels.

sanskrit: tān samīpagatāñ śrutvā niryayur vṛṣṇipuṃgavāḥ alaṃcakruś ca mālyaughaiḥ puruṣā nāgasāhvayam
english: Hearing that they had drawn near, the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis went forth to meet them, and the men adorned Hāstinapura with masses of garlands.

sanskrit: patākābhir vicitrābhir dhvajaiś ca vividhair api veśmāni samalaṃcakruḥ paurāś cāpi janādhipa
english: With many-coloured banners and with manifold flags the townsfolk too adorned their houses, O ruler of the people.

sanskrit: devatāyatanānāṃ ca pūjā bahuvidhās tathā saṃdideśātha viduraḥ pāṇḍuputrapriyepsayā
english: And worship of many kinds at the temples of the gods Vidura ordained, out of his wish to please the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: rājamārgāś ca tatrāsan sumanobhir alaṃkṛtāḥ śuśubhe tat puraṃ cāpi samudraughanibhasvanam
english: The royal highways there were decked with flowers, and the city shone, resounding like the surging of the ocean.

sanskrit: nartakaiś cāpi nṛtyadbhir gāyanānāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ āsīd vaiśravaṇasyeva nivāsas tat puraṃ tadā
english: With dancers performing their dances and with the singing of the minstrels, that city then was like the dwelling of Vaiśravaṇa.

sanskrit: bandibhiś ca narai rājan strīsahāyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ tatra tatra vivikteṣu samantād upaśobhitam
english: With its bards and men by thousands, accompanied by women, it was made beautiful on every side, here and there in its secluded places, O king.

sanskrit: patākā dhūyamānāś ca śvasatā mātariśvanā adarśayann iva tadā kurūn vai dakṣiṇottarān
english: The banners, shaken by the breathing wind, seemed then as if to point out the Kurus to the south and to the north.

sanskrit: aghoṣayat tadā cāpi puruṣo rājadhūrgataḥ sarvarātrivihāro 'dya ratnābharaṇalakṣaṇaḥ
english: And a man set at the head of the royal proclamation cried aloud then: "This day there shall be revelry all night long, marked by jewels and ornaments!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tān samīpagatāñ śrutvā pāṇḍavāñ śatrukarśanaḥ vāsudevaḥ sahāmātyaḥ pratyudyāto didṛkṣayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that the Pāṇḍavas had drawn near, Vāsudeva, the harrower of foes, went forth with his ministers, desiring to see them.

sanskrit: te sametya yathānyāyaṃ pāṇḍavā vṛṣṇibhiḥ saha viviśuḥ sahitā rājan puraṃ vāraṇasāhvayam
english: Having met together in due form, the Pāṇḍavas along with the Vṛṣṇis entered, all united, the city named after the elephant, O king.

sanskrit: mahatas tasya sainyasya khuranemisvanena ca dyāvāpṛthivyau khaṃ caiva śabdenāsīt samāvṛtam
english: And by the sound of the hooves and the chariot-wheels of that great host, heaven and earth and the sky were enveloped in the din.

sanskrit: te kośam agrataḥ kṛtvā viviśuḥ svapuraṃ tadā pāṇḍavāḥ prītamanasaḥ sāmātyāḥ sasuhṛdgaṇāḥ
english: Setting their treasure at the fore, the Pāṇḍavas then entered their own city, glad at heart, with their ministers and the bands of their friends.

sanskrit: te sametya yathānyāyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janādhipam kīrtayantaḥ svanāmāni tasya pādau vavandire
english: Approaching King Dhṛtarāṣṭra in due form, and proclaiming each his own name, they reverenced his feet.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrād anu ca te gāndhārīṃ subalātmajām kuntīṃ ca rājaśārdūla tadā bharatasattamāḥ
english: And after Dhṛtarāṣṭra those best of the Bharatas then saluted Gāndhārī, the daughter of Subala, and Kuntī, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: viduraṃ pūjayitvā ca vaiśyāputraṃ sametya ca pūjyamānāḥ sma te vīrā vyarājanta viśāṃ pate
english: And having honoured Vidura, and met with the son born of the Vaiśya woman, those heroes, themselves being honoured, shone forth, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tatas tat param āścaryaṃ vicitraṃ mahad adbhutam śuśruvus te tadā vīrāḥ pitus te janma bhārata
english: Then those heroes heard of that supreme wonder, strange and great and marvellous—the birth of your father, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad upaśrutya te karma vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ pūjārhaṃ pūjayām āsuḥ kṛṣṇaṃ devakinandanam
english: Hearing of that deed of the wise Vāsudeva, they honoured, as one worthy of honour, Kṛṣṇa, the joy of Devakī.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ ājagāma mahātejā nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Then, after a few days, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī, of great splendour, came to the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: tasya sarve yathānyāyaṃ pūjāṃ cakruḥ kurūdvahāḥ saha vṛṣṇyandhakavyāghrair upāsāṃ cakrire tadā
english: To him all the upholders of the Kurus did honour in due form, and together with the tigers of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas they then waited upon him.

sanskrit: tatra nānāvidhākārāḥ kathāḥ samanukīrtya vai yudhiṣṭhiro dharmasuto vyāsaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: There, when tales of many sorts had been recounted, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma spoke these words to Vyāsa:

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād bhagavan yad idaṃ ratnam āhṛtam upayoktuṃ tad icchāmi vājimedhe mahākratau
english: "By your grace, O blessed one, this treasure has been gathered; I wish to employ it in the great rite of the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: tad anujñātum icchāmi bhavatā munisattama tvadadhīnā vayaṃ sarve kṛṣṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: For this I desire your sanction, O best of sages; we are all dependent upon you and upon the great-souled Kṛṣṇa."

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca anujānāmi rājaṃs tvāṃ kriyatāṃ yad anantaram yajasva vājimedhena vidhivad dakṣiṇāvatā
english: Vyāsa said: "I grant you leave, O king; let what follows be done. Sacrifice with a horse sacrifice, performed according to rule and rich in priestly gifts.

sanskrit: aśvamedho hi rājendra pāvanaḥ sarvapāpmanām teneṣṭvā tvaṃ vipāpmā vai bhavitā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For the horse sacrifice, O lord of kings, is a purifier from all sins; having sacrificed therewith you shall surely be freed of sin—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tu dharmātmā kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ aśvamedhasya kauravya cakārāharaṇe matim
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the righteous Yudhiṣṭhira, king of the Kurus, O Kaurava, set his mind upon the undertaking of the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: samanujñāpya tu sa taṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ nṛpaḥ vāsudevam athāmantrya vāgmī vacanam abravīt
english: Having taken leave of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, the eloquent king then addressed Vāsudeva and spoke these words:

sanskrit: devakī suprajā devī tvayā puruṣasattama yad brūyāṃ tvāṃ mahābāho tat kṛthās tvam ihācyuta
english: "Blessed in her offspring is the lady Devakī through you, O best of men; whatever I may ask of you, O mighty-armed, do that here, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: tvatprabhāvārjitān bhogān aśnīma yadunandana parākrameṇa buddhyā ca tvayeyaṃ nirjitā mahī
english: It is enjoyments won by your power that we enjoy, O joy of the Yadus; by your valour and your wisdom this earth has been conquered.

sanskrit: dīkṣayasva tvam ātmānaṃ tvaṃ naḥ paramako guruḥ tvayīṣṭavati dharmajña vipāpmā syām ahaṃ vibho tvaṃ hi yajño 'kṣaraḥ sarvas tvaṃ dharmas tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
english: Consecrate yourself for the rite; you are our highest teacher. When you have offered the sacrifice, O knower of dharma, I shall be freed of sin, O lord; for you are the whole imperishable sacrifice, you are dharma, you are Prajāpati."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tvam evaitan mahābāho vaktum arhasy ariṃdama tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānām iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: "It is fitting, O mighty-armed, that you yourself should say this, O subduer of foes; that you are the refuge of all beings—such is my settled conviction.

sanskrit: tvaṃ cādya kuruvīrāṇāṃ dharmeṇābhivirājase guṇabhūtāḥ sma te rājaṃs tvaṃ no rājan mato guruḥ
english: And you today shine forth among the Kuru heroes by your righteousness; we are but your dependents, O king; you, O king, are deemed by us our teacher.

sanskrit: yajasva madanujñātaḥ prāpta eva kratur mayā yunaktu no bhavān kārye yatra vāñchasi bhārata satyaṃ te pratijānāmi sarvaṃ kartāsmi te 'nagha
english: Sacrifice with my sanction; the rite is as good as performed by me. Let your honour set us to the task wherein you desire it, O Bhārata; truly I promise you, I shall do all for you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: bhīmasenārjunau caiva tathā mādravatīsutau iṣṭavanto bhaviṣyanti tvayīṣṭavati bhārata
english: Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and likewise the two sons of Mādrī, shall be deemed to have sacrificed when you have sacrificed, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu kṛṣṇena dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vyāsam āmantrya medhāvī tato vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the wise Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, turned to Vyāsa and then spoke these words:

sanskrit: yathā kālaṃ bhavān vetti hayamedhasya tattvataḥ dīkṣayasva tadā mā tvaṃ tvayy āyatto hi me kratuḥ
english: "As you know truly the proper time for the horse sacrifice, then consecrate me; for upon you depends my rite."

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca ahaṃ pailo 'tha kaunteya yājñavalkyas tathaiva ca vidhānaṃ yad yathākālaṃ tat kartāro na saṃśayaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: "I, and Paila, O son of Kuntī, and likewise Yājñavalkya—we shall be the performers of the ordinance according to its proper times, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: caitryāṃ hi paurṇamāsyāṃ ca tava dīkṣā bhaviṣyati saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhriyantāṃ te yajñārthaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: On the full-moon day of Caitra your consecration shall take place; let the materials be gathered for the sake of the sacrifice, O bull among men.

sanskrit: aśvavidyāvidaś caiva sūtā viprāś ca tadvidaḥ medhyam aśvaṃ parīkṣantāṃ tava yajñārthasiddhaye
english: And let the charioteers skilled in the lore of horses, and the brāhmaṇas versed in it, examine a horse fit for the rite, for the accomplishment of your sacrifice's purpose.

sanskrit: tam utsṛjya yathāśāstraṃ pṛthivīṃ sāgarāmbarām sa paryetu yaśo nāmnā tava pārthiva vardhayan
english: Releasing it according to the scriptures, let it roam over the earth that is girdled by the sea, increasing your glory and your name, O king."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tathety uktvā pāṇḍavaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ cakāra sarvaṃ rājendra yathoktaṃ brahmavādinā saṃbhārāś caiva rājendra sarve saṃkalpitābhavan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the Pāṇḍava lord of the earth said "So be it" and did everything, O lord of kings, as the expounder of Brahman had said; and all the materials, O lord of kings, were made ready.

sanskrit: sa saṃbhārān samāhṛtya nṛpo dharmātmajas tadā nyavedayad ameyātmā kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāya vai
english: Having gathered the materials, the king, the son of Dharma, of immeasurable soul, then made his report to Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā vyāso dharmātmajaṃ nṛpam yathākālaṃ yathāyogaṃ sajjāḥ sma tava dīkṣaṇe
english: Then Vyāsa of great splendour said to the king, the son of Dharma: "At the proper time and in fitting manner we are ready for your consecration.

sanskrit: sphyaś ca kūrcaś ca sauvarṇo yac cānyad api kaurava tatra yogyaṃ bhavet kiṃ cit tad raukmaṃ kriyatām iti
english: Let the sacrificial ladle and the bundle of grass be of gold, O Kaurava, and whatever else there may be fit for the rite, let that be made of gold.

sanskrit: aśvaś cotsṛjyatām adya pṛthvyām atha yathākramam suguptaś ca caratv eṣa yathāśāstraṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: And let the horse be released today upon the earth in due order, and let it roam well-guarded according to the scriptures, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayam aśvo mayā brahmann utsṛṣṭaḥ pṛthivīm imām cariṣyati yathākāmaṃ tatra vai saṃvidhīyatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This horse, O brāhmaṇa, has been released by me; it shall roam this earth at its will. Therein let provision be made.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ paryaṭantaṃ hi turagaṃ kāmacāriṇam kaḥ pālayed iti mune tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Who should guard the horse as it wanders the earth, moving at its own pleasure—of this, O sage, your honour should speak."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tu rājendra kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt bhīmasenād avarajaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, O lord of kings, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana replied: "He who is younger than Bhīmasena, the foremost of all bowmen,

sanskrit: jiṣṇuḥ sahiṣṇur dhṛṣṇuś ca sa enaṃ pālayiṣyati śaktaḥ sa hi mahīṃ jetuṃ nivātakavacāntakaḥ
english: victorious, enduring, and bold—he shall guard it; for he is able to conquer the earth, he who made an end of the Nivātakavacas.

sanskrit: tasmin hy astrāṇi divyāni divyaṃ saṃhananaṃ tathā divyaṃ dhanuś ceṣudhī ca sa enam anuyāsyati
english: In him are the celestial weapons, and a celestial frame likewise, a celestial bow and two quivers; he shall follow after it.

sanskrit: sa hi dharmārthakuśalaḥ sarvavidyāviśāradaḥ yathāśāstraṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha cārayiṣyati te hayam
english: For he is skilled in dharma and in profit, accomplished in all learning; according to the scriptures, O best of kings, he shall cause your horse to roam.

sanskrit: rājaputro mahābāhuḥ śyāmo rājīvalocanaḥ abhimanyoḥ pitā vīraḥ sa enam anuyāsyati
english: The mighty-armed prince, dark of hue and lotus-eyed, the heroic father of Abhimanyu—he shall follow after it."

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi tejasvī kaunteyo 'mitavikramaḥ samartho rakṣituṃ rāṣṭraṃ nakulaś ca viśāṃ pate
english: "Bhīmasena too, the splendid son of Kuntī of boundless valour, is able to guard the kingdom, and Nakula as well, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu kauravya samādhāsyati buddhimān kuṭumbatantraṃ vidhivat sarvam eva mahāyaśāḥ
english: And Sahadeva, O Kaurava, the wise and greatly renowned, shall duly order the whole management of the household."

sanskrit: tat tu sarvaṃ yathānyāyam uktaṃ kurukulodvahaḥ cakāra phalgunaṃ cāpi saṃdideśa hayaṃ prati
english: All that, spoken in due form, the upholder of the Kuru line carried out, and he charged Phalguna with the matter of the horse.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ehy arjuna tvayā vīra hayo 'yaṃ paripālyatām tvam arho rakṣituṃ hy enaṃ nānyaḥ kaś cana mānavaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Come, Arjuna; by you, O hero, let this horse be guarded; for you are worthy to protect it, and no other man whatsoever.

sanskrit: ye cāpi tvāṃ mahābāho pratyudīyur narādhipāḥ tair vigraho yathā na syāt tathā kāryaṃ tvayānagha
english: And those kings who may come forth against you, O mighty-armed—so act that there be no strife with them, O sinless one.

sanskrit: ākhyātavyaś ca bhavatā yajño 'yaṃ mama sarvaśaḥ pārthivebhyo mahābāho samaye gamyatām iti
english: And this sacrifice of mine should be made known by you everywhere to the kings, O mighty-armed: 'Let them come at the appointed time.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā bhrātaraṃ savyasācinam bhīmaṃ ca nakulaṃ caiva puraguptau samādadhat
english: Having so spoken, the righteous one appointed his brother the ambidextrous archer—and Bhīma and Nakula—to the guarding of the city.

sanskrit: kuṭumbatantre ca tathā sahadevaṃ yudhāṃ patim anumānya mahīpālaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: And to the management of the household he appointed Sahadeva, the lord of warriors, after Yudhiṣṭhira had taken leave of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dīkṣākāle tu saṃprāpte tatas te sumahartvijaḥ vidhivad dīkṣayām āsur aśvamedhāya pārthivam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the time of consecration had come, those most eminent priests duly consecrated the king for the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: kṛtvā sa paśubandhāṃś ca dīkṣitaḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ dharmarājo mahātejāḥ sahartvigbhir vyarocata
english: Having performed the binding of the victims and being consecrated, the son of Pāṇḍu, the righteous king of great splendour, shone forth together with his priests.

sanskrit: hayaś ca hayamedhārthaṃ svayaṃ sa brahmavādinā utsṛṣṭaḥ śāstravidhinā vyāsenāmitatejasā
english: And the horse, for the sake of the horse sacrifice, was released according to the rule of scripture by the expounder of Brahman himself, by Vyāsa of immeasurable splendour.

sanskrit: sa rājā dharmajo rājan dīkṣito vibabhau tadā hemamālī rukmakaṇṭhaḥ pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ
english: That king, the son of Dharma, being consecrated, shone forth then, O king, garlanded with gold and golden-collared, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājinī daṇḍapāṇiḥ kṣaumavāsāḥ sa dharmajaḥ vibabhau dyutimān bhūyaḥ prajāpatir ivādhvare
english: Clad in a black antelope-skin, staff in hand, robed in linen, the radiant son of Dharma shone forth still more, like Prajāpati at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tathaivāsyartvijaḥ sarve tulyaveṣā viśāṃ pate babhūvur arjunaś caiva pradīpta iva pāvakaḥ
english: And so too all his priests were of like attire, O lord of the people; and Arjuna likewise was like blazing fire.

sanskrit: śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasāraṃ taṃ sasārāśvaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ vidhivat pṛthivīpāla dharmarājasya śāsanāt
english: Dhanaṃjaya of the white horses followed after that black-spotted steed, in due form, O guardian of the earth, at the command of the righteous king.

sanskrit: vikṣipan gāṇḍivaṃ rājan baddhagodhāṅgulitravān tam aśvaṃ pṛthivīpāla mudā yuktaḥ sasāra ha
english: Brandishing the Gāṇḍīva, O king, with leathern guard upon his fingers bound, he followed that horse, joined with gladness, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: ākumāraṃ tadā rājann āgamat tat puraṃ vibho draṣṭukāmaṃ kuruśreṣṭhaṃ prayāsyantaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then, O king, the whole city, down to the children, came forth, O lord, eager to behold the best of the Kurus, Dhanaṃjaya, as he was setting out.

sanskrit: teṣām anyonyasaṃmardād ūṣmeva samajāyata didṛkṣūṇāṃ hayaṃ taṃ ca taṃ caiva hayasāriṇam
english: From the press of them one against another there arose a kind of heat, as they longed to see both that horse and the follower of the horse.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahārāja daśāśāḥ pratipūrayan babhūva prekṣatāṃ nṝṇāṃ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then a clamour arose, O great king, filling the ten quarters, from the men gazing upon the son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: eṣa gacchati kaunteyas turagaś caiva dīptimān yam anveti mahābāhuḥ saṃspṛśan dhanur uttamam
english: "There goes the son of Kuntī, and there the radiant steed which the mighty-armed one follows, his hand upon his peerless bow!"

sanskrit: evaṃ śuśrāva vadatāṃ giro jiṣṇur udāradhīḥ svasti te 'stu vrajāriṣṭaṃ punaś caihīti bhārata
english: Thus did the victorious one of noble mind hear the words of those who spoke: "Blessing be upon you; go unharmed and come again!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāpare manuṣyendra puruṣā vākyam abruvan nainaṃ paśyāma saṃmarde dhanur etat pradṛśyate
english: And yet others, O lord of men, the men said these words: "We cannot see him in the crush; only this bow can be seen.

sanskrit: etad dhi bhīmanirhrādaṃ viśrutaṃ gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ svasti gacchatv ariṣṭaṃ vai panthānam akutobhayam nivṛttam enaṃ drakṣyāmaḥ punar evaṃ ca te 'bruvan
english: For this is the famed Gāṇḍīva bow of terrible roar. May he go in safety along a road unharmed and free from all fear; we shall behold him again upon his return"—thus too they spoke.
